αἰδέομαι: αἰδέομαι — feel shame, be ashamed (to do something); pres. 1 sg. mid./dep., + inf.: ’I am ashamed’
αἰειγενέτῃσι: αἰειγενέτης — ever-born, everlasting (of the gods); adj., masc. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι (= Attic -αις), agreeing with θεοῖς
αὐτῆς: αὐτός — self; fem. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive (τὰ σ’ αὐτῆς ἔργα ’your own works’): ’of yourself’ · also plain gen. sg. governed by ἄγχι ’near, close to’: ’her’ (ἄγχι δ’ αὐτῆς ’close beside her’) · also plain gen. sg. pronoun ’it’ (of a ship, fem.), governed by a noun: χρεὼ ... αὐτῆς ’a need of it’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun ’it’ (of a raft, fem.), governed by a preposition: ἐπ’ αὐτῆς ’upon it’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun ’her’, possessive with a noun: νόος ... αὐτῆς ’her mind’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun ’her’, governed by a preposition, of a monster: ἀπ’ αὐτῆς ’away from her’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun ’it’ (of the olive), governed by ἀγχόθι ’near’: ἀγχόθι δ’ αὐτῆς ’and near it’ · also intensive with a noun, fem. gen. sg.: αὐτῆς Ἰθάκης ’Ithaca itself’ · also ὁ αὐτός ’the same’, fem. gen. sg. with the article: τῆς αὐτῆς ἀγγελίης ’the same news’ · also reflexive intensive gen. sg. after a personal pronoun, of a woman speaking: ἐξ ἐμεῦ … αὐτῆς ’from me myself’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun ’it’ (of a chair), after ἐκ: ἐξ αὐτῆς ’out of it’
βοῆς: βοή — shout, cry; fem. gen. sg., gen. of what is heard (with ἀίοντες): ’hearing the cry’
γέ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle, accented γέ before a following enclitic
γοῦνα: γόνυ — knee; neut. acc. pl., epic γοῦνα (= Attic γόνατα)
δεσμὸν: δεσμός — bond, fetter; masc. acc. sg.
δούλιον: δούλιος — of a slave, of slavery; neut. acc. sg.
δόμοισιν: δόμος — house, home; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις), plural for a single dwelling
δώῃ: δίδωμι — give, grant; aor. subj. 3 sg. (= Attic δῷ), after αἴ κε: ’may grant’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a general relative clause, without κε: ’gives, is to give’ (οἵ τ’ … βῶσιν καί σφι Ζεὺς … δώῃ) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a prospective relative clause with κε: ’who shall give’ (ὅς κ’ … τάμῃσι … δώῃ) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’may give’ (ὄφρα … δώῃ γέρας ’so that he may give a prize’) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in the protasis after εἴ κε, continuing a preceding subj.: ’grants’ (εἴ κέ μιν ἐντανύσῃ, δώῃ δέ οἱ εὖχος ’if he strings it, and grants him glory’)
εἴπῃσιν: εἶπον — say, tell; aor. subj. 3 sg., epic -ῃσιν (ν-movable, = Attic εἴπῃ)
θείῃ: τίθημι — put, place, make; aor. subj. 3 sg., epic θείῃ (= Attic θῇ); with σκέδασιν, ’bring about’
κραιπνοῖσι: κραιπνός — swift, rushing; masc. dat. pl., epic -οῖσι (= Attic -οῖς)
κρατερὴ: κρατερός — strong, mighty, harsh; fem. nom. sg.
κτείνας: κτείνω — kill, slay; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ‘having killed’
κόμιζε: κομίζω — take care of, tend; pres. imper. 2 sg.
κύσε: κυνέω — kiss; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔκυσε)
λόφον: λόφος — ridge, crest of a hill; masc. acc. sg.
μετά: μετά — after, next to; prep. + acc. (accented before the enclitic γε): ’after’
νοήσας: νοέω — perceive, understand; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having perceived’
νομὸν: νομός — pasture, grazing ground; masc. acc. sg.
πεφυγμένον: φεύγω — flee, escape; perf. part. mid./pass. masc./neut. acc. sg.: ’having escaped’ (with εἶναι, ’has escaped’)
σεύατ: σεύω (mid. σεύομαι) — dart, rush, speed; aor. mid. 3 sg., unaugmented, elided (σεύατ’ = σεύατο): ’sped, darted’
σοῦ: σύ — you (sg.); gen. sg.: ’of you, your’
σῆς: σός — your, yours (sg.); possessive adj., fem. gen. sg.
τεθνηῶτα: θνῄσκω — die; perf. part. masc. acc. sg., epic (= Attic τεθνεῶτα): ’dead’
τοιοῦδ: τοιόσδε — such as this; masc. gen. sg., elided (τοιοῦδ’ = τοιοῦδε)
τροίης: Τροία — Troy; gen. sg. (Ionic -ης for Attic -ας)
τῇσιν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. pl., epic (= Attic ταῖς): ’them’ · also fem. dat. pl. ’at them, at which’, of the mills (τῇσιν … ἐπερρώοντο γυναῖκες ’at which the women worked’)
φίλου: φίλος — dear, one’s own; masc. gen. sg.
χώρης: χώρη — place, spot (Ionic; Attic χώρα); fem. gen. sg.
ἀγαθόν: ἀγαθός — good; neut. acc. sg.: ’good, a good thing’ · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal passive (κακόν τ’ ἀγαθόν τε τέτυκται ’whatever, good or bad, has come to pass’)
ἀμφιπόλους: ἀμφίπολος — handmaid, attendant; fem. acc. pl.
ἀμύνειν: ἀμύνω — ward off (+ acc. of what is warded off); pres. inf. act.
ἀνιόντα: ἄνειμι — come back, go up; pres. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’on his way back’
ἀπορρήξας: ἀπορρήγνυμι — break off, tear off; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having torn off’
ἀρνύμενος: ἄρνυμαι — strive to win, earn; pres. part. nom. sg. masc.
ἄλλοισίν: ἄλλος — other; adj., masc. dat. pl.: ’to the others’
ἄχνυται: ἄχνυμαι — be grieved, be distressed; pres. 3 sg. mid.
ἐγέλασσε: γελάω — laugh; aor. 3 sg., epic σσ (= ἐγέλασε): ’laughed’
ἐγγεγάασιν: ἐγγίγνομαι — be born in, dwell in; perf. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἐγγεγόνασιν): ’have been born in, live in’
ἐναίσιμον: ἐναίσιμος — fitting, in due measure; neut. acc. sg.
ἐναίσιμος: ἐναίσιμος — fitting, right, according to due measure; masc./fem. nom. sg. (built on αἶσα ’due share’)
ἐοῦσα: εἰμί — be; pres. part. fem. nom. sg., epic ἐοῦσα (= Attic οὖσα)
ἐποίχεσθαι: ἐποίχομαι — go about, ply (a task); pres. inf.
ἐσσύμενον: σεύω — drive, hurry; mid./pass. rush, hasten; perf. part. mid./pass., masc. acc. sg., epic doubled σ: ’eager to go’
ἑόν: ἑός, ἑή, ἑόν — his own, her own (possessive, = ὅς); masc. acc. sg., with ἄνακτα: ’her own (lord)’; not the relative
ἔτετμεν: τέτμον (defective aor., ‘find, come upon’) — find; aor. 3 sg.: ‘he had found’
ἔφαντο: φημί — say; mid. ’think, suppose, believe’; impf. mid. 3 pl.: ’they supposed’ · also mid. ’said, declared, promised’, + fut. inf. (ἔφαντο ἄξειν ’they said they would bring’)
ἤθεα: ἦθος — accustomed place, haunt; neut. pl. ἤθεα, acc.: ’usual places’
ἱστόν: ἱστός — loom; masc. acc. sg. · also ’mast’ (of a ship), a distinct sense required by nautical context (ἐν δ’ ἱστόν τ’ ἐτίθεντο ’they set the mast in it’)
ἵξεσθαι: ἱκνέομαι — come to, reach, arrive at; fut. inf. mid. (ἵξομαι), after ἔμελλε: ’to be about to reach’
ὑπότροπον: ὑπότροπος — returning, back home; masc. acc. sg.: ’returned’
ὑψηλοῖσι: ὑψηλός — high, lofty; adj., masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οῖς)
